title: National Cycling League
body:
A rider's speeds over n checkpoints are given. For a window length d, look at every block of d consecutive checkpoints, take the maximum speed in each block, and report the smallest of those maxima. Answer q such queries.

Also seen as "Customer Satisfaction Analysis".

Function to complete

Complete answerQueries(speeds, queries). It returns one answer per query.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: n q. Line 2: the n speeds. Next q lines: d.

samples.ex: With d = 3 the window maxima are 85 90 95 100 100, so the answer is 85. With d = 4 they are 90 95 100 100, so 90.

py.pre:
from typing import *
import sys, math, collections, heapq, bisect, itertools, functools
from collections import *
py.post:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _q = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    speeds = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_n)])); _p += (_n)
    queries = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_q)])); _p += (_q)
    _r = Solution().answerQueries(speeds, queries)
    print("\n".join(map(str, _r)))
